Experiments on multiple challenging benchmarks demonstrate consistent and substantial performance gains, while ablation and efficiency studies further validate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed design.
Additional case studies are provided in Appendix  A.3 . 
 Limitations 
 Despite the demonstrated effectiveness of MemoBrain across multiple benchmarks, several limitations remain that are important to acknowledge. 
 (1) MemoBrain assumes that the underlying reasoning agent is capable of sustained, long-horizon tool use and iterative reasoning. However, many current LLMs tend to terminate reasoning prematurely after a limited number of tool calls, often drawing conclusions before sufficient evidence is collected. In such cases, the accumulated context does not reach the threshold required to trigger memory management, and MemoBrain has little opportunity to intervene. We observe this limitation in experiments with both Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507-Instruct and Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507-Thinking, where early termination restricts the practical benefits of executive memory. 
 (2) While the memory graph maintained by MemoBrain naturally supports richer cognitive operations inspired by human memory, such as reactivating previously flushed reasoning episodes or partitioning the memory graph for parallel exploration, this work focuses on only two core operations: folding and selective flush. These design choices are intended to isolate the fundamental effects of executive memory control. Exploring more advanced memory operations and their coordination remains an important direction for future work. 
 (3) Our experimental comparison does not include all potentially relevant baselines. Some memory-augmented methods are designed mainly for long-context settings and cannot be readily adapted to dynamic reasoning trajectories. Others lack public implementations or require computational resources beyond our constraints. Additionally, our reproduced results for DeepResearch-30B-A3B on GAIA and WebWalker are slightly lower than those reported in the original paper, partly due to differences in tool implementations (e.g., search quality and code execution). Nevertheless, all comparative experiments are conducted under identical settings, ensuring that the relative improvements by MemoBrain remain valid and meaningful.
